correctness.rationale: Original next-generation matrix reconstructed from the exact source equations. Population-diagonal similarity gives explicit symmetric H(p). Its normalized characteristic polynomial Q is reproduced exactly in the standalone verifier. Q_z>0 on the Perron root, L(0)=1, L′(0)=-r(1-a), and Q_pp=-2r(1-a)(1-b)(L-a)<0 at that root. Therefore every critical point is a strict minimum and two such points are impossible. Endpoint derivative Q_p(1)=(1-a)(3a-2)/4, with positive endpoint curvature when it vanishes, gives sharp alpha=2/3. Exact resultant and substitution determine pstar and the two invasion fractions; the smaller eigenvalue cannot be the 10/11 branch. This is an analytic argument for all claimed parameters. Finite numerical tests are not used as proof. p=1 only a matrix limit; no original-model claim at p=1.

value.rationale: The all-population-ratio unimodality lemma settles whether more one-way commuting can re-increase invasion risk, a natural unresolved question after the source’s metropolitan R0 bounds and mobility histograms. The exact alpha=2/3 crossover differentiates optimal partial commuting from the unattainable fully commuting limit. With beta1/(gamma+mu)=11/10 and alpha=0, two exact commuting thresholds create a genuine re-entrant disease-invasion classification, motivating targeted mobility policy. This is a structural result and threshold boundary, not a small arbitrary numeric gain or a renaming of a textbook eigenvalue inequality.
